Docusign Envelope ID: 54883297-3298-4333-B1F5-EB792CF7BDFD Revised 10/02/2024 MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING BETWEEN THE NASHVILLE FIRE DEPARTMENT AND THE METROPOLITAN DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY SERVICES TO FULFILL A GIS POSITION FOR THE NASHVILLE FIRE DEPARTMENT
1. BACKGROUND and PURPOSE The mission of the Nashville Fire Department (NFD) is to provide high quality fire, medical, and rescue emergency responses and community support services to the citizens and visitors within Nashville and Davidson County, so they can work and reside in a community where an all-hazard response minimizes harm to life, property and environment. The Metropolitan Government of Nashville and Davidson County (Metro) Information Technology Services Department (ITS) provides technology solutions to Metro entities and manages centralized enterprise systems that serve 60 Metro departments and agencies. Geospatial information provides decision makers the ability to display, manipulate and analyze critical information to enable wiser decision making, and has provided solutions in areas such as environmental protection, land use, transportation, public safety, and emergency management. With Geographic Information Systems (GIS), analytics specialists can create visualizations, identify meaningful trends, and make predictions. The GIS program is also responsible for educating Metro leaders on the capabilities that GIS technology can provide to enhance operational efficiencies and support the goals of their department. For example, Esri has out of the box solutions for Target Hazard Analysis, Special Event Operation, Pre-Incident Planning that were designed for use by Fire and Emergency Response agencies. Metro’s enterprise GIS platform, depicted in the high-level architecture diagram below, was designed with a dedicated, segmented Health/Fire GIS portal intended to meet HIPAA data sensitivity requirements. Metro’s GIS program has the necessary enterprise GIS platform built, enterprise licensing acquired, an enterprise governance policy approved by the CAL Steering Committee, and the skilled staff to support the program for Metro. Docusign Envelope ID: 54883297-3298-4333-B1F5-EB792CF7BDFD Revised 10/02/2024 Despite the growing significance of geospatial information and technology, many Metro Government organizations are not yet able to fully leverage the extent of benefits this technology can offer. An increased level of knowledge, skills, and abilities in the workforce, along with improved technology and data accuracy, will be required for Metro departments to fully utilize the capabilities this technology can offer. Having program support at the highest level is a critical and foundational component of any enterprise program, but the benefits that can be realized with GIS technology is much more powerful when there is a blend of highly specialized GIS skillset with domain level expertise.
2. PROPOSAL The purpose of this memorandum of understanding between NFD and ITS is to define the terms that will result in the fulfillment, onboarding, training, and oversight of one contract to hire position for the purpose of expediting the implementation and adoption of GIS tools and technologies across NFD. a. Phase One There is currently an existing and unfilled FTE within the NFD Fire Marshal’s office that NFD commits to keep unfilled and reserved for a full time GIS Analyst as a part of this agreement. ITS requires the position classification to be a minimum of an IS Analyst 3 to hire and retain a candidate with the necessary skillset to perform the job duties. As such, NFD will classify the position in accordance with ITS’s needs. ITS will be responsible for compiling a job description, coordinating with recruitment agencies, interviewing candidates, and selecting the candidate for the position. ITS commits to work through Metro’s recruitment agencies to fill this role with a contract to hire position. ITS commits to creating a Purchase Order (PO) and will be responsible for coordinating monthly payments to the recruitment agency of the selected candidate. NFD agrees to provide funding for this PO from business unit 32116310. November 1, 2024 is the target start date for this position, though it is possible that this position will begin prior to or after October 1st depending on the skillset and availability of the candidates that apply. The one-time equipment cost to purchase computer equipment will be funded by NFD, and this equipment will be permanent NFD assets. Any ITS purchased equipment will be permanent assets of ITS. b. Phase Two As a part of the Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) budget process, ITS and NFD will include the transfer of the IS Analyst 3 from NFD to ITS with an associated salary of $85,000. The effective date of the transfer will be July 1, 2025. ITS will post an open competitive job announcement in accordance with Metro Civil Service Rules and Policies to hire the IS Analyst 3 position as a full-time employee (FTE) after the FTE transfer to ITS is complete and a minimum of six months of satisfactory performance has been completed by the contracted candidate. This position will be eligible to receive any compensation Page 2 of 6 ARCHIVE
Docusign Envelope ID: 54883297-3298-4333-B1F5-EB792CF7BDFD Revised 10/02/2024 adjustments applied to the IS Analyst 3 classification. Additionally, this position will be included in any applicable job specific compensation studies while working for the ITS department. c. Phase Three In the middle of the fiscal year 2026, representatives from NFD and ITS will meet and discuss whether the IS Analyst will remain an employee of ITS or be transferred to NFD. There is no obligation or expectation that this position will remain an ITS position after the conclusion of FY26. There is, however, the expectation that NFD and ITS will evaluate the candidate’s performance, assignment complexity and scope of stakeholders involved in their planned work for the upcoming year, and their ability to work independently as factors in the decision. If NFD and ITS decide that it would be in the best interest of both departments for this IS Analyst position to remain an ITS position in order to gain an additional year of experience working with ITS’s central GIS team in support of implementing solutions for NFD, the FTE will not be transferred for FY27. NFD and ITS will meet in the middle of FY27 to make the determination regarding the FTE transfer back to NFD for FY28. When NFD and ITS determine that the IS Analyst position should to transferred back to NFD, then ITS and NFD will include the transfer of the IS Analyst 3 and associated salary from ITS to NFD as a part of the upcoming Fiscal Year budgeting process. The effective date of this transfer will be July 1 of the agreed upon fiscal year. ITS would continue to support NFD as needed through its standard support offerings. The IS Analyst 3 FTE or equivalent contractor will be an employee of or contracted to the ITS department, reporting to the GIS Division Manager. ITS commits to onboarding this employee with their standard onboarding processes and practices and providing training on Metro’s enterprise GIS platform and Metro GIS data assets. The GIS Division Manager will have full autonomy for providing all supervisory responsibilities, including performance evaluations as a member of the GIS & Data Insights team and commits to prioritizing work assignments that support the needs of NFD, with Fire Marshall work having top priority. The ITS GIS Manager will establish a regular meeting quarterly with the Fire Marshal and the ITS Assistant Director to provide a status update of specific work assignments, to receive any new work assignments from discuss progress of the position overall, and discuss any concerns. The primary intent of these meetings is to keep all stakeholders updated and involved and to make any adjustments as needed to support the long-term success of this position. ITS commits to providing a trained backup for this MOU IS Analyst position, providing a layer of redundancy and risk mitigation. The MOU IS Analyst position will also be trained to provide backup support for portions of Metro’s GIS program. The person in this MOU IS Analyst position is expected to participate in all relevant NFD and ITS meetings, and to proactively work with NFD staff to develop and implement a prioritized work plan of solution implementations and activities to support the expanded use of GIS and data analysis across NFD. There will be times when NFD will want this person to physically report to work at NFD, which ITS agrees is important, and will allow the person to physically report. ITS requests that NFD + New assignments and priority realignment can occur at any time by request from the Fire Marshal. Page 3 of 6 ARCHIVE

NFD will require that the candidate make their Outlook calendar available to both NFD and ITS management for streamlined coordination of in-person attendance at NFD. Primary responsibilities for this IS Analyst position include (specific to supporting NFD’s use of GIS), but are not limited to: e Work closely with end users to conduct use-case analysis of business functions to identify GIS application requirements, technical issues, and training needs. e Conduct use-case analysis of business functions to establish GIS application requirements and geospatial data model requirements for customers. ¢ Communicate with internal and external technical resources to resolve end-user issues and provide guidance to users on methods for correcting problems. e Identify and define appropriate applications of the system and associated GIS products e Participate in compatibility testing of application upgrades (planning, development, user testing, implementation) of GIS web applications / desktop extensions to keep pace with current platform version. e Perform quality control processes on GIS data and attribute information. e Plan and communicate specific work tasks for database creation and management, application development, and ongoing maintenance. e Prepare technical documentation including data specifications, user requirements, and procedures. Produce maps showing the spatial distribution of various kinds of data. Produce reports on geographic data utilizing data visualizations. Perform spatial analysis of both vector and raster datasets. Conduct in-house training and tracking progress on system implementation and application projects. Understanding of the data, functions, and tasks that the GIS applications will support. e Configure Esri solutions within ArcGIS Enterprise Portal, utilizing products such as Field Maps and Survey 123. e Researches and develops solutions to difficult issues and presents alternatives to management. e Provide technical support with third-party integration products. e Review literature, consult with experts, and coordinate with vendors to identify appropriate hardware and/or software solutions to complex problems. e Receive direction and report to a top departmental manager, who is consulted on unusual or complex matters. e Perform other related duties as assigned by ITS in support of NFD. As part of this agreement, this staff member will be required to follow all ITS departmental policies and procedures. This includes an initial Criminal Justice Information Security (CJIS) background check required of new ITS employees and maintaining a “passing” status on CJIS background checks. Failure to maintain a passing status will lead to disciplinary action for an employee or release from contract for a contractor. Page 4 of 6 ARCHIVE
